summary: Federation Logistics is a family-run third-party logistics and warehousing operator at 149 Black Horse Lane in North Brunswick, NJ, offering warehousing, kitting, drayage from the NY/NJ ports, transportation and customs-bonded plus liquor-licensed storage from New Jersey and California. Its own site claims 500,000 sq ft of combined warehouse/rack space, 4 NJ locations, and counters for roughly 100k pallets and 55k containers a year; federal records show 15 power units and 16 drivers. The commercial front door is a single ~70-field quote form labelled Customer Survey, or a phone call to a main line - with no booking, portal or acknowledgement path.

facts.fact: Company describes itself as a warehousing and distribution / 3PL provider in California and New Jersey serving the East Coast, with over 500,000 sq ft of combined warehouse and rack space and customs-bonded facilities.

Service lines listed on the home page: Warehousing, Kitting and projects, Drayage, Transportation, Bonded warehouse, Liquor Licensed warehouse; the certifications block lists FDA, USDA, UIIA, US Customs, SQF and ABC (Alcoholic Beverage Control).
Published contact details: 149 Black Horse Lane, North Brunswick, NJ 08902; (732) 422-4090; info@fedlogistics.com; footer hours Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:30pm.
Site hours are inconsistent: footer says Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:30pm, the mobile menu says Mon-Fri 8:00-6:00, and the Port Authority warehouse directory lists 0800-1700.

Quote intake is one long form headlined Customer Survey: company/contact block plus inbound, storage, outbound and communication sections including 12 monthly volume fields, pallet specs, batch/lot sensitivity and EDI percentages, submitted by a single Send message button that posts back to quote.php.
The form records that verbal orders are not accepted at the warehouse: order channels are captured as percentages of EDI/electronic, fax, e-mail or other, with the note Verbals not accepted.
Top navigation items About us, Services and Contact all point to #, so no about, service or contact page exists on the live site; robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return 404.
The mobile menu still contains the template placeholder: the visible text info@fedlogistics.com is wrapped in a mailto:help@company.com link.

FMCSA SAFER Company Snapshot for FEDERATION DISTRIBUTION SERVICES INC, USDOT 935795, MC-553031, at 149 Black Horse Lane, N Brunswick NJ 08902, phone (732) 422-4090: USDOT active, authorized for-hire motor carrier of property, interstate, 15 power units, 16 drivers, MCS-150 dated 05/06/2026, 631,480 miles reported for 2025; 3 driver inspections in the prior 24 months, 0 crashes.

Port Authority of NY & NJ warehouse directory (October 2023 edition) lists Federation Logistics, North Brunswick 08902, over 100,000 sq ft, hours 0800-1700, food-grade, commodity food products, contact Roberto Ruiz at 732-422-4090.

2016 Association of Bi-State Motor Carriers member profile: President and founder Les Sokoloff started the company in Brooklyn in the late 1960s; co-owner and VP of Operations Frank Touma joined in 1977; then a 100,000 sq ft North Brunswick HQ plus 150,000 sq ft owned across the street plus leased NJ space; customers were import/export businesses shipping clothing, canned goods, olive oil, water and sugar; the company ran a drayage fleet serving NY/NJ/PA and a daily shuttle van for Brooklyn staff after the New Jersey move.

Federation Distribution Services Inc signed a 104,451 sq ft industrial lease at 461 Ridge Road, South Brunswick NJ, occupying half of a newly renovated building on a 65-month term (JLL for the landlord Woodmont Industrial Partners/Sagard, Lee & Associates for the tenant).
Home-page counters in the page source report 4 locations across NJ, over 100k pallets handled per year and 55k containers picked up from NJ ports, but render as 0 until the counter script runs.

The page sets maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=0, and the stylesheet hides the address/e-mail/hours bar below 1023px and hides the header phone button below 1439px, so a phone visitor sees no phone number until the hamburger menu is opened.

operations_signals: Two intake routes only: a phone call to (732) 422-4090 or the quote.php form; no online booking, customer portal, document upload or acknowledgement page was found (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

Quote intake requires the prospect to complete a ~70-field survey (12 monthly volume percentages, SKU counts, pallet grades, batch/lot sensitivity, EDI/fax/e-mail mix) before any human conversation, so staff must read and re-key it into whatever holds the rate build (https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php)
The form header is still Customer Survey and it carries legacy-era fields (fax number, % fax orders, pallet grades) - a paper quote sheet transcribed to web (https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php)

The warehouse will not take verbal orders; order intake is expected as EDI, fax, e-mail or other, which concentrates exception handling on a small back-office group (https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php)

Hours are stated three different ways (site footer 8:00am-4:30pm, mobile menu 8:00-6:00, Port Authority directory 0800-1700); no after-hours, weekend or holiday coverage is published anywhere (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

Drayage runs on 16 drivers under the related carrier authority, with Call Anytime language in the header but no dispatch desk, shipment tracking or self-serve appointment scheduling published (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?searchtype=ANY&query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=935795)
No careers page, no supplier/vendor page and no document upload for customs or ABC paperwork; the only document-adjacent channel is the info@ mailbox (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
Social links (Twitter/Facebook/Instagram) in the header and footer all resolve to #, so there is no monitored social inbox (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
hiring_signals: No current job postings found on the company site (there is no careers page) or on public job boards; searches for warehouse, dispatcher and clerk roles at Federation Logistics returned only aggregator pages with no live listings (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Federation-Logistics)

Role mix implied by the operating model rather than by postings: 16 drivers plus warehouse, kitting and back-office order entry for bonded and liquor-licensed accounts (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?searchtype=ANY&query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=935795)

Historical retention claim from a 2016 trade profile: many staff and drivers with 20+ years of service, and a daily shuttle van run for Brooklyn-based staff after the move to New Jersey - consistent with referral hiring over board hiring (https://www.bistatemotorcarriers.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Newsletter-2016Apr.pdf)

Employer-review footprint is tiny and stale (Indeed 1.5/5 from 2 reviews, both January 2014; Glassdoor 2.8/5 from 6 reviews dated 2015-2018), so there is no current public signal on staffing strain; both pages returned 403 when opened directly (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Federation-Logistics/reviews?fcountry=ALL)
review_themes: No customer reviews were located on any public source reached in this pass; a directory listing shows the business with no reviews, and review aggregators for the address were blocked (https://www.whereorg.com/federation-logistics-10719363)

Employee reviews are the only public voice: 2 Indeed reviews averaging 1.5/5, both from January 2014, describing demanding conditions with one note on diversity; too old and too few to read as a current signal (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Federation-Logistics/reviews?fcountry=ALL)

Glassdoor shows 2.8/5 across 6 reviews dated 2015-2018; the page could not be opened (403), so themes beyond the score were not read (https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Federation-Logistics-Reviews-E462621.htm)

The company's own marketing carries the service claim - a president quote about treating customers' goods as its own, 40 years and 45 years of experience in the same paragraph, and the line Hundreds of customers trust our company - but no testimonials, case studies or named clients are published (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
tech_footprint: Static PHP site on a purchased logistics HTML template, with a Revolution Slider hero, animated counters, jQuery, Bootstrap 5 and SweetAlert2 for form feedback; no CMS, blog, news or resource section (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

No CRM, chat widget, booking widget, quote calculator, tracking portal or customer login on either live page; the only interactive elements are the quote form and a Google Maps embed (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

The quote form is a plain HTML POST back to quote.php with client-side validation and a single-quote ban on free-text fields (an SQL-escape workaround), suggesting hand-built server handling rather than a form platform (https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php)

No JSON-LD/LocalBusiness schema, no meta description, page title is only the company name, and the sole H1 is Hundreds of customers trust our company with no town, service or warehouse keyword (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
Carrier integrations appear only as UPS and FedEx logos; the site names no WMS, TMS, EDI translator or inventory-visibility tool (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

The footer credits an individual developer and the site still ships template placeholder assets, consistent with handoff maintenance rather than an in-house marketing function (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
growth_signals: November 2024: 104,451 sq ft lease at 461 Ridge Road, South Brunswick (half of a renovated 210,000 sq ft building, 65 months) - a step change in NJ square footage and a new site to staff and coordinate (https://rebusinessonline.com/federation-distribution-services-signs-104451-sf-industrial-lease-in-south-brunswick-new-jersey/)
Own site claims 4 NJ locations and 500,000+ sq ft combined, up from 450,000 sq ft in a 2016 trade profile - consistent with the 2024 South Brunswick lease (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

Federal filing freshness: MCS-150 updated 05/06/2026 and 631,480 miles reported for 2025, so the carrier side is actively maintained and operating (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?searchtype=ANY&query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=935795)

Heritage and tenure are core sales assets (40 years on the home page, 45+ years in body copy, founded in Brooklyn in the late 1960s), and the firm is a member of the Association of Bi-State Motor Carriers (https://www.bistatemotorcarriers.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Newsletter-2016Apr.pdf)
No awards, press releases, new-service launches or leadership changes were found for 2025-2026 (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
physical_signals: North Brunswick HQ at 149 Black Horse Lane, described in 2016 as a 100,000 sq ft headquarters building plus another 150,000 sq ft of owned warehouse directly across the street, plus leased warehouse space elsewhere in NJ (https://www.bistatemotorcarriers.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Newsletter-2016Apr.pdf)

Port Authority warehouse directory: the North Brunswick site is over 100,000 sq ft, food-grade, food products, open 0800-1700 (https://aemdev.panynj.gov/content/dam/port/our-port/council-on-port-performance-pdf/available-warehouse-space.pdf)

New 104,451 sq ft footprint at 461 Ridge Road, South Brunswick NJ, in a newly renovated 210,000 sq ft building (https://rebusinessonline.com/federation-distribution-services-signs-104451-sf-industrial-lease-in-south-brunswick-new-jersey/)

Fleet: 15 power units and 16 drivers under USDOT 935795, interstate for-hire general freight; the company says its sites are 30 miles from the ports (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?searchtype=ANY&query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=935795)
Storage modes described as rack and bulk, with bonded and liquor-licensed (ABC) areas, FDA/USDA/SQF food-grade handling, and kitting/project space (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)

Safety record on file: 3 driver inspections in the 24 months to 11/11/2026, 0 out-of-service, 0 crashes, no safety rating issued (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?searchtype=ANY&query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=935795)
Port throughput counters on the site: over 100k pallets per year and 55k containers picked up from NJ ports to its facilities (company marketing figures, unverified) (https://www.fedlogistics.com/)
decision_maker: Les Sokoloff, President (also described as founder) - named in the site's own hero quote and in the Association of Bi-State Motor Carriers 2016 member profile (https://www.fedlogistics.com/, https://www.bistatemotorcarriers.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Newsletter-2016Apr.pdf). Second named principal: Frank Touma, co-owner and VP of Operations, in the same 2016 profile (may be dated). Business contact in the Port Authority directory: Roberto Ruiz, (732) 422-4090.

inferences.inference: Federation Logistics, LLC and Federation Distribution Services Inc are the same operating business under two legal names.
inferences.reasoning: The FMCSA record for USDOT 935795 sits at the same street address and phone number as the website, and the 2024 South Brunswick lease was signed by Federation Distribution Services Inc while the website and phone line are used for both brands.

inferences.inference: Quote turnaround is a manual bottleneck likely measured in days, not minutes.
inferences.reasoning: Every inbound lead arrives as free-text form data or a phone call into a Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30 office, has to be reconciled against pallet/SKU/monthly-volume detail, and there is no auto-acknowledgement, CRM or scheduling tool visible on the site.

inferences.inference: A meaningful share of quote-form starts are probably abandoned before submission.
inferences.reasoning: The form demands warehouse-ops detail (pallet grade percentages, batch vs lot sensitivity, EDI mix, 12 monthly volume percentages) that a prospect often cannot answer without their own ops team, and on mobile there is no visible phone fallback in the header until the hamburger menu is opened.

inferences.inference: Bonded, liquor-licensed and food-grade work creates recurring document and compliance chores handled by people rather than systems.
inferences.reasoning: The company advertises US Customs bonded, ABC liquor-licensed and SQF/FDA/USDA scopes, yet publishes no portal, upload, appointment or document-request flow; the only channels offered are the form and the info@ mailbox.

inferences.inference: Growth is coming from leased satellite warehouses, which raises coordination load faster than headcount.
inferences.reasoning: The 2024 South Brunswick lease of 104,451 sq ft plus the claim of 4 NJ locations means inventory, dock appointments and driver dispatch now span multiple sites, while the public-facing systems still describe one North Brunswick address and one phone line.

inferences.inference: Hiring runs on referrals and longevity rather than job boards.
inferences.reasoning: There is no careers page and no live public postings, while a 2016 profile describes 20-year tenures and a shuttle service used to retain Brooklyn staff; this is a network-hiring pattern (inference, not stated by any source).

inferences.inference: The website is in reactive maintenance, not under active marketing ownership.
inferences.reasoning: Nav links point to #, a template placeholder e-mail link survives in the mobile menu, robots.txt and sitemap.xml are missing, there is no meta description or schema, social links are dead, and hours contradict each other across page sections.

inferences.inference: Public reputation data is too thin to benchmark service quality either way.
inferences.reasoning: No customer reviews were found on any reachable source and the only ratings located (Indeed, Glassdoor) are employee reviews from 2014-2018; in a B2B warehouse context low review volume reflects buyer behaviour, not necessarily service quality.

data_gaps: Google Business Profile could not be re-checked: Maps is JavaScript-only and this task had no browser tool. The triage record cites a 3.6 rating with no review count; treat that number as unverified.

Indeed, Glassdoor, Yellowpages, dot.report, carrieratlas, re-nj.com and OSHA's inspection detail page all returned HTTP 403, so their contents were only seen as search-result snippets, not read directly.
No current or recent job postings were found for this employer on any board, so hiring-strain signals rest on role inference rather than actual postings.
No customer reviews, testimonials or case studies exist on any reachable source; review_themes is therefore thin and mostly employer-side.
The 390px phone rendering could not be captured without a browser; mobile conclusions come from reading the HTML and responsive.css rather than a rendered screenshot.

The Port Authority warehouse directory used is the October 2023 edition and its hours (0800-1700) conflict with the site (8:00am-4:30pm), so current hours and whether the North Brunswick site is currently customs-bonded remain unconfirmed.
Square footage is self-reported and inconsistent across years (450,000 sq ft in 2016, 500,000+ now, 100k+ in the Port Authority listing); no authoritative per-site figure was found.
Employee headcount is unverified; a directory estimate of 50-99 employees was not confirmable and no LinkedIn company headcount was accessible.
